subject: AcmeFin evals: recommended models, prompt set, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <s.kim@acmefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeFin discovery — recommended models, prompt set, next steps

Hi Sarah — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so the team is aligned: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- Primary use case: customer support triage + draft responses for transactional financial inquiries.
- Throughput target: ~200 reqs/min at 95th percentile latency < 600ms.
- Quality: high factual accuracy, strict PII handling / redaction.

Recommended model variants to try on Redwood for the evals:
1) redwood-13b-v2 (quantized) — best balance of latency/cost for high throughput; start here as a baseline.
2) redwood-70b-realtime (8-bit) — for higher quality on complex completions; will cost more but we expect improved accuracy on edge cases.
3) open-llama-13b-finetuned (customer prompt-tuned) — lower cost alternative for controlled routing.

Attached: acmefin_prompt_set_v1.csv — a first-pass prompt set derived from the call and your sample transcripts. Format note below.

Eval setup proposal (what Redwood will run):
- Sandbox project in your org (isolated) with a dedicated eval key.
- You provide 1-2 representative datasets (CSV preferred). We recommend: input, expected_output, category, pii_flag.
- Scoring: top-1 exact match + token-level F1 for entity extraction + semantic similarity (embedding cosine) for open answers. We'll provide thresholds and sample scripts.
- Review cadence: we run 3 model variants across the prompt set and provide a per-case breakdown, latency/cost report, and recommended routing policy.

Immediate asks from AcmeFin:
1) Confirm you'll share the canonical test dataset (CSV) and mark any PII-sensitive rows.
2) Confirm a 2-week target window for the initial eval run (we can start as early as Tue 7/14).
3) Any compliance constraints for sandbox (e.g., IP allowlist, region, KMS)?

Attachments: acmefin_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV; 3.1 KB)

Next steps: if you confirm dataset share and the 7/14 start, Neha will provision the sandbox and Marcus will own model-run configs. I'll follow up with a meeting invite to review results.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Kim <s.kim@acmefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Ortiz <d.ortiz@acmefin.com>, procurement@acmefin.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeFin discovery — recommended models, prompt set, next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Sarah here (Head of AI at AcmeFin). A couple quick clarifications before we share the dataset: 

1) PII handling: we'll need the sandbox to be in us-west (we cannot move data to eu regions) and an IP allowlist. Can Neha confirm that is supported?
2) Dataset format: the attached CSV looks good — we'll add a pii_flag column and mask any account numbers in expected_output. Is that the preferred approach?
3) Scoring: can you confirm how you compute "semantic similarity"? We prefer reproducible metrics — what library/embedding model do you use for that?

Procurement looped in for timing/po terms. Our target is to run the first pass between 7/14–7/16 and review results on 7/17 if that works on your side.

Thanks,
Sarah

> Hi Sarah — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so the team is aligned:
> ...
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <s.kim@acmefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeFin discovery — recommended models, prompt set, next steps

Hi Sarah — happy to confirm the technical bits.

1) Region/IP/KMS: we can provision the sandbox in us-west (us-west-2). IP allowlisting is supported; we'll send the allowlist template. For KMS, we offer customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; for hosted evals we can enable envelope encryption and audit logs.

2) Dataset format (recommended CSV schema):
- header row required
- columns: id, input, expected_output, category, pii_flag (values: yes/no), notes
- max rows for initial pass: 2,000 (we can scale up once the harness is validated)

3) Semantic similarity: we compute embedding-based cosine similarity using the redwood-embed-2 model (public embedding checkpoint). For reproducibility we will provide: the embed model name, embedding dimension, vector normalization, and the threshold used per test category. We also provide a per-case visualization so you can inspect low/high matches.

4) Scoring script + rubric: attached redwood_eval_playbook.pdf — includes exact-match rules, token-F1 for entity extraction, and embedding thresholds for loose vs strict matches. We'll also surface a precision/recall breakdown for NER-like tasks.

Attachments: redwood_eval_playbook.pdf (PDF; 220 KB)

Action items for AcmeFin:
- Share the CSV with pii_flag populated and masked expected_output for any rows with account numbers.
- Send the IP ranges to allowlist (we'll provide our endpoints).

We can schedule the sandbox provisioning for Mon 7/13 morning and start the run 7/14. Marissa — should I go ahead and provision?

Thanks,
Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
